To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed an approach to numerically compute QNMs for the Klein-Gordon equation on doubly rotating Myers-Perry black hole spacetimes.
we have developed the first full numerical approach to finding QNMs of doubly rotating Myers-Perry black hole in arbitrary dimension.
we have found a full numerical approach for the computation of the Quasinormal Modes of a class of black holes in $D\ge 6$ dimensions with two independent rotation rates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of Quasi-Normal Mode (QNMs) for doubly rotating black hole backgrounds.
the study of the QNMs of the most general black hole in higher dimensions.
the study of the Quasi-Normal Mode spectrum of black hole perturbations in higher dimensional spacetime with multiple rotation parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a numerical and perturbative approach to find the QNMs for a general class of black holes.
we have a full and accurate numerical approach to find the QNMs of any $D\ge 6$ dimensional doubly rotating black holes for any value of the rotation parameters and all other angular quantum numbers.
the QNMs of doubly rotating Myers-Perry black hole are in general not the same as those of a singly rotating Myers-Perry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have obtained a full numerical approach for the radial part of the QNMs and a perturbative expansion up to second order in the rotation parameters for the angular part of the QNM frequencies of doubly rotating black holes in arbitrary dimensions.

we find a full set of QNMs for the scalar, electromagnetic and gravitational perturbations for $D=6,7,8$ and $9$ for both the Kerr-AdS and Kerr-dS black holes, and a full set of scalar QNMs for $D=10,11$ and $12$ for the Kerr-Ad$S$ black hole.

we provide an explicit expression for the metric for doubly rotating black hole in arbitrary dimension, and a complete numerical approach for the computation of the radial part of the QNM for arbitrary dimension, and an explicit perturbative expansion for the angular quantum number up to second order for $D\ge 6$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QNMs of doubly rotating Myers-Perry black hole can be obtained from the QNMs for a single rotating Myers-Perry by using a suitable transformation.
, for $D\ge 6$ and slow rotation, there is a simple relationship between the QNMs and the angular quantum numbers.
